$comment: Reviewer registry for this repository — a port of dotfiles/harness/review-attestation.json,
trimmed to the reviewers that measurably act here. Precedent for a per-repo port: kubelab,
hive, web and ts-bridge each carry their own copy; the SSOT of the SHAPE stays in dotfiles.
Why the port was needed: this file did not exist, so `dotf pr triage-queue` could not answer
at all — `read reviewer registry: open harness/review-attestation.json: no such file or
directory`. Its exit status is 1 both when triage is pending AND when the question cannot be
computed, precisely so an unanswerable queue is never mistaken for a clear one. But a check
that reports the same thing every time it runs stops being read, which is how a gate degrades
into noise. Ported 2026-09-06 from the ts-bridge copy (ts-bridge #311).
review_markers ARE MEASURED HERE, NOT COPIED. Measured 2026-09-06 over the 12 most recent PRs
`gh api repos/mlorentedev/iris/issues/<n>/comments`, classifying each coderabbitai[bot] body:
## Walkthrough            -> all 11 non-dependabot PRs (#21-#26, #28, #31, #33, #39, #44);
a review ran; this is the attesting marker
No actionable comments    -> #24 #31 #33 #44 (always inside a Walkthrough comment, so it
adds nothing as a marker and is deliberately NOT declared)
## Review limit reached   -> 0 PRs
rate limited by coderabbit.ai -> 0 PRs
## Review skipped         -> 0 PRs
(no CodeRabbit output)    -> #35 (dependabot)
Addendum, same day: #46 (opened right after the measurement) drew `## Review limit reached`
with 'You've used all free OSS reviews for now', so the first declined marker IS now observed
here. The declined_markers below are kept for that reason and because a declined marker that
never fires is inert (the queue reads `pending` either way), whereas a review marker that never
fires would report every PR as clear forever. The strings are the ones ts-bridge measured on the
same vendor; `rate limited by coderabbit.ai` has not been observed in iris.
Note the asymmetry that survives this: a CodeRabbit run that files ONLY a formal review with no
walkthrough comment still reads as 'no reviewer output yet'. That is a property of the tool, which
scans comments, and it is why pr-stewardship still asks a human to read the diff. Measured on
#44: CodeRabbit filed both a Walkthrough comment and a COMMENTED review, so the comment path is
the one that attests.
The `github-actions` entry declares an actor that is about to exist rather than one that was
observed: pr-agent.yml landed in the same PR as this file, and its NAN_API_KEY secret is set by
`dotf secrets sync ci --repo mlorentedev/iris` after the dotfiles registry PR lands. Read the
entry's own `why` for what has and has not been verified.
No `exempt` block: this repository runs no release-please (no .release-please-manifest.json,
no CHANGELOG.md), so there is no diff signature to exempt. Add one only with a measurement.

reviewers.why: ADVISORY, same disposition as the dotfiles, kubelab and ts-bridge registries: its REVIEW attests, its DECLINE does not refuse. CodeRabbit's quota is a third party's billing state rather than a property of the change. In this repo no decline has been observed yet (0 of 11 reviewed PRs, measured 2026-09-06), but the vendor's quota is shared across the account and ts-bridge measured a 59 % decline rate on the same plan, so a decline that REFUSED would turn a billing event into a red gate. An advisory decline yields `pending`, the honest answer: a reviewer that could not run is not a reviewer that refused. LOGINS MATCH WITH TRAILING '[bot]' STRIPPED AND CASE FOLDED, because the two GitHub APIs disagree: REST reports coderabbitai[bot], GraphQL reports coderabbitai. The dotfiles 'No actionable comments were generated' review marker is deliberately NOT reused -- see the $comment on review_markers.

PR-Agent (see .github/workflows/pr-agent.yml) runs under GITHUB_TOKEN and publishes through the COMMENTS api, so its reviews never enter reviews[] and a classifier that looked only at reviews would read every PR-Agent-reviewed PR as unattested. The marker is the `review` command's own heading. `## PR Code Suggestions` is deliberately NOT here — suggestions are not a review, which is also why auto_improve is off on the automatic path. MARKER PROVENANCE: verified in the sibling ports before being declared here — kubelab has 215 PR comments carrying '## PR Reviewer Guide' posted by github-actions[bot] and dotfiles has 172 (counted at ts-bridge #315). It has NEVER been observed in iris, because this workflow has not run here and NAN_API_KEY is not yet set in this repository: the first green run of pr-agent on an iris PR is the verification, and until then this entry is a declaration of intent, not of an actor.

triage.why: The heading the pr-review-triage skill records its dispositions under, matched at line start. Declared once here and read back by `dotf pr triage-queue`, so the writer and the reader are not a two-file agreement nobody checks. A disposition that lives only in a chat message evaporates, and the Definition of Done's Review item would then rest on a claim nobody can re-read. It is posted even when there was nothing to dispose of: 'CI green, no review findings' is a disposition, and leaving it unwritten is indistinguishable from nobody having looked. Already in use here before this file existed: #44 carries one.

escape.label: merged-unreviewed
escape.why: Both are required, never one. Proceeding on an unreviewed PR is allowed; proceeding SILENTLY is not. The label plus the section is what forces the disclosure into the durable record instead of a chat message.
